You are part of an optimization system that improves a given text (i.e. the variable). You are the gradient (feedback) engine. Your only responsibility is to give intelligent and creative feedback and constructive criticism to variables, given an objective specified in <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> </OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> tags. The variables may be solutions to problems, prompts to language models, code, or any other text-based variable. Pay attention to the role description of the variable, and the context in which it is used. You should assume that the variable will be used in a similar context in the future. Only provide strategies, explanations, and methods to change in the variable. DO NOT propose a new version of the variable, that will be the job of the optimizer. For instance, feedback can be in the form of 'Since language models have the X failure mode...', 'Adding X can fix this error because...', 'Removing X can improve the objective function because...', 'Changing X to Y would fix the mistake ...', that gets at the downstream objective.
If a variable is already working well (e.g. the objective function is perfect, an evaluation shows the response is accurate), you should not give feedback.

# - <LM_OUTPUT>: The output of the language model.
# - <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION>: The objective of the optimization task.
# - <VARIABLE>: Specifies the span of the variable.
# - <ROLE>: The role description of the variable.
payload.instruction: Make her close her jacket fully
payload.rubric: Judge requested image editing: yes means all requested changes are complete, no means no requested change has progressed, partial means some progress without complete fulfillment. Unrelated edits are not requested progress. Insufficient evidence stays unresolved.

node.question: Is her jacket fully closed?
node.criteria: Compare the corresponding front closure areas of the same jacket in SOURCE and EDITED. Score concrete movement of the front panels toward each other as partial fulfillment when a visible opening remains; score full fulfillment only when the panels meet along the closure and no visible opening remains. If turning, draping, or occlusion prevents a reliable comparison of the closure areas, leave fulfillment unresolved rather than treating poor visibility as no progress or inferring progress from pose or motion.
node.binding: Compare the jacket on the woman in SOURCE with the jacket on the woman in EDITED, focusing on corresponding visible portions of its front closure. Judge the requested endpoint as a fully closed jacket; distinguish visible partial closure from no change, and use insufficient evidence when the closure cannot be reliably compared.
node.endpoint: Her jacket is fully closed, with no visible opening along the closure.
node.necessity: This is the requested change and its complete endpoint.
node.zero_when: The corresponding closure areas are sufficiently visible to compare, and the EDITED jacket shows no concrete movement of its front panels toward closure relative to SOURCE.
node.half_when: The corresponding closure areas show concrete movement of the front panels toward each other relative to SOURCE, but a visible opening remains; if the closure cannot be reliably compared, leave the score unresolved instead of assigning partial fulfillment.
node.full_when: The EDITED jacket’s front panels meet along the closure, with no visible opening remaining along it.

node_traces.evidence: In SOURCE, the jacket’s front is visible and appears open. In EDITED, she has turned and the jacket is swinging or draped away from her body, obscuring the corresponding front closure. The panels cannot be reliably compared, so closure progress and whether it is fully closed cannot be determined.

response.content: {"text":"The node correctly avoids inferring closure from the turn or swinging jacket, but its binding and criteria make the decision depend on comparing corresponding front panels even when the edited pose changes their visibility. In these images, SOURCE shows the jacket front open; EDITED shows her turned away, with the jacket flaring/draping and the closure not clearly visible. That is insufficient visual evidence—not evidence of no progress, and not a transport, schema, or dependency failure. Preserve the unresolved outcome when the closure is genuinely obscured; do not force the reference label or infer closure from motion. For robustness, clarify that the node should inspect any directly visible closure cues in EDITED independently as well as compare views, and distinguish a visible closed endpoint from mere occlusion. If no such cue is visible, retain uncertainty. The high-confidence unknown is a signal to review whether the criterion is over-dependent on cross-image correspondence, not grounds to relax the full-closure requirement."}
